chunks: He holds the keys of the heavens and the earth. He expands the provision for whom He wills and constrains it. Indeed, He is Knowing of all things.

key_terms.مَقَالِيدُ: Keys (plural of miftah, indicating control or authority)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Allah holds the keys of the heavens and the earth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores Allah's absolute dominion over the heavens and earth, serving as a foundation for understanding divine decree (Qadr) and the distribution of sustenance (Rizq). It highlights that while provision is expanded or constricted by His will, it is always rooted in His comprehensive knowledge, reassuring believers of the wisdom behind both ease and hardship. This concept is often linked to the idea that true Rizq is not merely material but includes spiritual guidance and well-being, known only to Allah.
